question: How many days of annual leave do full-time employees get?
expected_answer: 28 days a year, including bank holidays (more with long service, up to 30).
ai_answer: Full-time employees receive 28 days of paid annual leave each leave year, including bank holidays. Long-service days are added: 1 extra day after 3 years' continuous service (29 days in total) and 2 extra days after 5 years' continuous service (30 days in total), with a maximum entitlement of 30 days.

question: When do we get paid?
expected_answer: Monthly, on the last working day of the month.
ai_answer: Employees are paid monthly, on the last working day of the month. Payslips are available in StaffHub. Night shifts between midnight and 06:00 are paid at an enhanced rate of time and a quarter.

question: How long is the probation period for new starters?
expected_answer: 6 months, with reviews at 3 and 6 months; can be extended by up to 3 months.
ai_answer: New employees have a 6-month probation period, with review meetings held by their manager at 3 months and 6 months. Probation may be extended by up to 3 months if more time is needed.

question: What is the mileage rate if I use my own car for work?
expected_answer: 45p per mile (normal commuting can't be claimed).
ai_answer: Mileage in a personal car for company business is paid at 45p per mile under the Expenses Policy (P1). Normal commuting to your usual workplace cannot be claimed.

question: How long does my password need to be?
expected_answer: At least 14 characters, with MFA wherever supported.
ai_answer: Passwords must be at least 14 characters long, according to the Information Security Policy (v2025.1, §1-5). Passwords must also never be shared, written down or reused across systems.

question: How quickly must a customer complaint be acknowledged?
expected_answer: Within 2 working days (final response within 8 weeks).
ai_answer: A customer complaint must be acknowledged within 2 working days, according to the Customer Complaints Procedure (v2025.1), §1-7. The final response must be sent within 8 weeks.

question: How much company sick pay do I get if I've worked here for 4 years?
expected_answer: 4 weeks at full pay in any rolling 12 months (after probation), on top of SSP.
ai_answer: If you have between 3 and 5 years' length of service (which includes 4 years), you receive 4 weeks of company sick pay at full pay, in any rolling 12-month period. This applies after you have completed probation, and company sick pay tops up SSP to full basic pay.

question: What support can I get for studying a qualification?
expected_answer: Course fees up to £1,000 a year and up to 5 days' paid study leave, after probation.
ai_answer: Employees who have passed probation can apply through LearnHub for study support for a qualification relevant to their role. This covers course fees of up to £1,000 per year and up to 5 days of paid study leave per year for exams and study. Applications must be approved by the line manager and the Head of Learning and Development. If you leave within 12 months of a course finishing you must repay 100% of the course fees, and if you leave 12 to 24 months after it finishes you must repay 50%.

question: If I leave 18 months after the company paid for my course, do I have to pay anything back?
expected_answer: Yes, 50% of the course fees (leaving between 12 and 24 months after the course).
ai_answer: Yes. If you leave between 12 and 24 months after your course finishes, you must repay 50% of the course fees. The policy measures this from when the course finishes, not from when the company paid the fees, so if your course finished 18 months before you leave, 50% applies. The passages do not say how the 18-month period is counted if the course ran over a long period.

question: Is there an allowance for working from home?
expected_answer: £26 a month for employees contracted to work remotely at least 1 day a week.
ai_answer: Yes. Employees whose contract says they work remotely at least 1 day a week receive a home working allowance of £26 a month, paid through payroll (Remote and Workplace Policy, §4-7 and §-5). The passages do not say how the allowance applies to employees who work remotely less than that or who are not on a remote contract.

question: Can I roll over unused holiday into next year?
expected_answer: Yes, up to 8 days, which must be used by 30 June.
ai_answer: Yes, up to 8 days of unused annual leave can be carried forward into the next leave year without needing approval. Carried-forward days must be used by 30 June of the new leave year, and any not used by then are lost and not paid. Employees may carry forward more than 8 days only in limited cases, such as long-term sickness, maternity, paternity, adoption or shared parental leave, or business reasons where the manager cancelled approved leave and the Head of People approved in writing; in those cases up to 20 days may be carried forward, with sickness-related days usable within 18 months of the end of the leave year in which they were earned and other exceptional days by 30 June.

question: I clicked a dodgy link in an email. What should I do?
expected_answer: Report it to the IT Service Desk immediately (and use Report Phish for suspicious emails).
ai_answer: The passages do not cover clicking suspicious links in emails or any specific steps for phishing. The IT Acceptable Use Policy says you can contact the IT Service Desk through StaffHub or on extension 4357 to report a problem, so that is the route to use. The passages do not say what further steps to take, so check with the IT Service Desk for guidance.

question: Can I keep the tips a punter gives me at the blackjack table?
expected_answer: No. Gaming staff tips go in the tronc box and are shared through the tronc scheme.
ai_answer: No. Gaming employees must never keep tips personally. All tips given to gaming employees are placed in the tronc box at the table and shared through the tronc scheme (Code of Conduct, §1-4). Hospitality employees follow their venue's tipping process instead.

question: How quickly do I have to report a lost company laptop?
expected_answer: Immediately, and in any case within 1 hour, to the IT Service Desk.
ai_answer: A lost or stolen company device, including a laptop, must be reported to the IT Service Desk immediately, and in any case within 1 hour of noticing it. Reporting quickly allows the device to be wiped remotely.

question: What happens to my annual leave if I'm ill while I'm on holiday?
expected_answer: With a fit note, those days count as sickness and the leave is given back. Report it on day one.
ai_answer: If you are ill during booked annual leave and provide a fit note covering the days of sickness, those days are treated as sickness absence and the annual leave is returned to you. You must report the sickness on the first day, following the sickness reporting steps in section 2 of the policy.

question: Where do I report a customer I think is laundering money?
expected_answer: Directly to the MLRO with the internal suspicious activity report form, not SafeLog; never tell the customer.
ai_answer: Do not report suspected money laundering in SafeLog and do not discuss it with the customer or with colleagues who do not need to know. Report it directly to the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) using the internal suspicious activity report form, as described in the Compliance Guidelines, and send it on the same day. Do not investigate yourself and do not tell the customer, as tipping off is a criminal offence.

question: Can I claim my course fees back on expenses?
expected_answer: No. Course fees are paid directly by the company under the Training Policy.
ai_answer: No. Course fees are paid directly by the company and must not be claimed as expenses (Training and Development Policy, and the Expenses Policy also lists training course fees as non-claimable). Only travel and accommodation for approved training are claimed under the Expenses Policy.

question: Someone on the gaming floor looks under 18. What do I do?
expected_answer: Ask for photo ID (Think 25), tell the duty manager immediately, and log it before the end of the shift.
ai_answer: Ask the person for valid photo ID under Think 25 and tell the duty manager immediately, because nobody under 18 may enter the gaming floor. Then log the incident in SafeLog before the end of your shift.

question: Can gaming floor staff take two weeks off over Christmas?
expected_answer: No. 24 Dec to 1 Jan is a peak period; at most 5 consecutive days, and only with the General Manager's approval.
ai_answer: No. The period from 24 December to 1 January is a peak period. During peak periods, gaming floor and security employees may take no more than 5 consecutive days of leave, and only with approval from the General Manager of their venue. Two weeks off over Christmas would therefore exceed the limit. The passages do not say whether any other exception applies.

question: How much notice do I need to give to book a week of annual leave?
expected_answer: Twice the length of the leave, so 10 days for 5 days of leave; later if the rota is already published.
ai_answer: You must give notice of at least twice the length of the leave you request, made through StaffHub. For example, 5 days of leave needs at least 10 days' notice. A full week of 7 calendar days would therefore need at least 14 days' notice before the first day of leave. If you are a gaming floor or security employee, rotas are published 4 weeks in advance, and requests made after a rota is published can only be approved if cover is available. During peak periods (24 December to 1 January and listed sporting weekends), gaming floor and security staff may take no more than 5 consecutive days without the venue General Manager's approval. The passages do not say how a 'week' is counted if it includes non-working days, so check with your manager if that matters.

question: How much annual leave can I carry forward?
expected_answer: Up to 8 days, used by 30 June (the 2024 rule of 5 days by 31 March no longer applies).
ai_answer: Employees can carry forward up to 8 days of unused annual leave into the next leave year without needing approval; these must be used by 30 June of the new leave year, or they are lost and not paid (P3). A higher carry-forward of up to 20 days is only allowed in limited cases: long-term sickness, maternity, paternity, adoption or shared parental leave, or business reasons where the manager cancelled approved leave and the Head of People approved the exception in writing (P2). Days carried forward because of sickness must be used within 18 months of the end of the leave year in which they were earned, and other exceptional carry-forward must be used by 30 June (P2, P1).

question: How many days a week can office staff work from home?
expected_answer: Up to 2 days with manager agreement; Tuesday and Wednesday are office days (not 3, as in 2023).
ai_answer: Employees in office-based support roles (for example Finance, HR, IT, Compliance and Marketing) may work remotely for up to 2 days a week, with their line manager's agreement. Tuesday and Wednesday are anchor days when office-based employees are expected to be in the office unless on leave or agreed otherwise with their manager.

question: Am I allowed to work from abroad for a few days?
expected_answer: Office-based staff can, for up to 10 working days a year, with manager and Information Security approval in advance.
ai_answer: Yes, but only if you are in an office-based support role. Those employees may work from outside the UK for up to 10 working days in a calendar year. Each trip must be approved in advance by your line manager and the Information Security team, and requested through the IT Service Desk at least 2 weeks before travel. Venue roles such as gaming floor, cage, security, hospitality and customer service are performed on site and cannot be done remotely, so the policy does not provide for them to work from abroad. The passages do not say what happens if a request is refused. While working remotely, you must use a company laptop and the company VPN.
